origins.section: A Concurrent Add Is Seen or Missed by Where It Lands, So Walking and Then Clearing Loses Writes
A Walk Hands Out Entries Read Earlier, So Act on One with remove(key, value)
Each Element Comes at Most Once, but an Element Added Again Is a New One
size() and a Walk Answer at Different Moments

recorded.prompt:q-replica-count: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-replica-count: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-replica-count: Lines 35-38: "All three runs printed 473. The table is an array of bins ... the iterator goes through it bin by bin. A key that lands in a bin already passed is missed, and one that lands ahead is seen. Timing only decides where the walk is when the add lands." The determinism of the rerun is backed by 473 in all three runs.
recorded.prompt:q-window-cleanup: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-window-cleanup: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-window-cleanup: Lines 128-129: "remove(id) removes whatever the id maps to by then, and 431 times that was a session that had reconnected after the check." Lines 131-132 make the condition explicit (a reconnect puts a new record), which matches the immutable Window replaced on every request.
recorded.prompt:q-moved-task: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-moved-task: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-moved-task: Lines 139-141: the CLQ javadoc's exactly-once promise covers elements "contained in the queue since the creation of the iterator", and "An element removed and added again was not contained the whole time." Lines 154-155: "The walk returned job-1407, then met its retried copy at the tail." Lines 160-163 (key 1 put back comes again) support the same-identity case. The page's retrier moves a Job with a raised attempt count, not the identical object, but the section heading and the map example cover re-adding the same value.
recorded.prompt:q-mapping-count: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mapping-count: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mapping-count: Lines 181-182: "When the map grew after size(), the walk overran the array." Line 186: "keySet().toArray(new String[0]) takes the length from its own walk." Line 213: "mappingCount() returns a long estimate". Together these decide that swapping in mappingCount still takes the count before the walk.

recorded.prompt:q-replica-count:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-replica-count:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-replica-count:a: Refuted by lines 35-37: "All three runs printed 473" and "Timing only decides where the walk is when the add lands". In the stem the walk waits at a fixed point, so the bins decide and the result does not depend on how the puts were ordered.
recorded.prompt:q-replica-count:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-replica-count:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-replica-count:c: Refuted only indirectly. Lines 9-10 give 'walks the array it started with' as the CopyOnWriteArrayList behavior and contrast it with weakly consistent iterators, and line 37 says a key landing ahead "is seen". The page never mentions resizing, so the 'keys before the resize' framing is not addressed directly. Weak but sufficient.
recorded.prompt:q-replica-count:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-replica-count:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-replica-count:d: Refuted by line 36: "A key that lands in a bin already passed is missed", and by the 473-of-1000 result. Lines 38-39 limit 'seen if it lands before the iterator reaches the last element' to the queue.
recorded.prompt:q-window-cleanup:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-window-cleanup:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-window-cleanup:a: Lines 11-12 quote the javadoc: weakly consistent iterators "will never throw ConcurrentModificationException". The Reference table also says 'never'.
recorded.prompt:q-window-cleanup:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-window-cleanup:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-window-cleanup:b: Refuted only indirectly. The page never names IllegalStateException. Line 128 says remove(id) "removes whatever the id maps to by then", and the code at line 106-107 (`Session gone = sessions.remove(...); if (gone != null)`) shows it returns a value and does not throw. Line 2 notes that no walk has ever thrown.
recorded.prompt:q-window-cleanup:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-window-cleanup:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-window-cleanup:c: Refuted by lines 95-96 ("An entry from a walk is a reading from some time during the walk, not the mapping now") and lines 128-129 (431 reconnected sessions removed). PARTLY TRUE: the option's first half is accurate, since the cleanup can remove the Window it checked. Only 'and none newer' is false.
recorded.prompt:q-moved-task:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-moved-task:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-moved-task:a: Refuted by the heading 'an Element Added Again Is a New One' and lines 140-141. The once promise is per element contained the whole time, not per object.
recorded.prompt:q-moved-task:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-moved-task:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-moved-task:b: Refuted by lines 154-155: the walk met the retried copy at the tail even though the retrier took the job off before putting it back. PARTLY TRUE: the premise that the queue never holds it twice is accurate. Only the conclusion is wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-moved-task:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-moved-task:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-moved-task:d: Refuted only implicitly. Line 38 says "A queue's iterator follows the links from head to tail, and an add goes on the tail", which describes a single pass, and lines 154-155 put the repeat down to the retried copy at the tail. The page never says outright that the walk does not restart.
recorded.prompt:q-mapping-count:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mapping-count:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mapping-count:a: Refuted by Reference line 213, which says size() is an estimate and "mappingCount() returns a long estimate". Lines 183-186 quote the javadoc on size being for estimation only.
recorded.prompt:q-mapping-count:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mapping-count:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mapping-count:c: Refuted only indirectly. Line 213 calls it an estimate, and the heading/summary ("size() and a walk answer at different moments"; "Count what the walk returned") imply that a count is a single reading. The page never says in so many words that mappingCount() doesn't follow the walk.
recorded.prompt:q-mapping-count:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mapping-count:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mapping-count:d: Mostly refuted by line 95 ("the element existed when the walk began") and Reference line 210 ("removed after the walk read ahead to it"), with lines 181-182 placing the overflow on growth. AMBIGUITY: in the page's own demo (lines 83-91) `ann` is removed after the iterator is created but before the first next(), and is still returned. A reader who takes 'before it started' to mean before the first element is returned could find d partly true. The answer direction ('No') is also correct in d, so only its reason distinguishes it from b.
